claims.text: Kestrel is the default web server for ASP.NET Core apps.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Servers: Kestrel overview

claims.text: Kestrel turns bytes arriving on a TCP connection into a request object, and a code decision back into response bytes.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Kestrel: HTTP server implementation

claims.text: Kestrel by itself has no routes and no business logic; it only accepts connections and produces request/response objects for other code.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Kestrel: when to use Kestrel with a reverse proxy

claims.text: The stage-0 Caddyfile's handle @postOrder block always answers POST /api/v1/orders with the fixed body {"id":13,"customer_id":1,"status":"new"}, status 201 and header Location: /api/v1/orders/13, which tells the client where the new order lives.
The stage-0 Caddyfile's handle @getOrder block always answers GET /api/v1/orders/1 with the fixed body {"id":1,"customer_id":1,"status":"paid"} and status 200.
Both respond bodies in the quoted Caddyfile block are literal strings, so respond sends that exact text back on every matching request.
claims.source_hint: Caddy docs, respond directive and Caddyfile concepts (placeholders)

claims.text: Running scripts/http/methods.sh twice against the stage-0 stack prints Location: /api/v1/orders/13 both times for the POST request.
Kestrel runs inside a single app process; it does not by itself spread requests across several machines, so stopping that process makes every request to its port fail.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Kestrel: when to use a reverse proxy

claims.text: Listening on a port only accepts a TCP connection; parsing the bytes into well-formed HTTP is separate work Kestrel performs. A program that reads the bytes, then closes the connection without writing a response, makes curl report 'Empty reply from server'.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs, Kestrel: HTTP server implementation
